mode: Independent read-only source and author regression-log review. No test, producer, Cargo, dotnet, consumer or network action executed by this reviewer.
decision: SOURCE_GO: the identified premature overall-success blocker is closed by this exact delta. Normal CI may execute the existing B24 acceptance path.
scope: Two files only: release_cases.py receipt state/terminal commit correction and a focused orchestration regression. No package graph, package/native bytes, product request behavior, accepted prior results, comparison thresholds or public publication scope changed.
checks: A new output directory is required. Initial result and every completed-case progress write use passed=false/status=running; successful individual cases cannot advertise overall completion.
Exceptions, subprocess failures and KeyboardInterrupt are not converted into success. Prior nonterminal receipts remain false even if a later operation fails or the process stops.
Terminal completion requires the exact eleven existing case names, exact count and every case passed is True; missing, duplicated or unexpected cases fail the guard.
All required journals/catalogs are copied before completion. The evidence index is atomically written before either terminal result is exposed.

The index binds the future completed result hash from model.json_bytes; the existing release.atomic_json uses identical sorted/indented UTF-8 JSON plus newline, so the indexed digest describes the actual terminal bytes.

Evidence result is committed first and the top-level result is the final orchestration commit marker. A reader must combine the actual process/CI exit and authoritative top-level marker with evidence integrity; partial progress does not constitute B24 acceptance.

The focused test invokes the real release main and its receipt writes with explicitly documented publication/consumer boundary stubs. It tests orchestration persistence, not product or package acceptance.

cases: Consumer RuntimeError after the first partial-publication case preserves both receipts as false/running and no completed index.
Consumer KeyboardInterrupt after the first case preserves incomplete receipts.
Index write failure after all eleven cases preserves both receipts as false/running.
Successful main path keeps all earlier writes false; only the final evidence/top-level writes are true, both receipt bytes agree and all indexed hashes are checked.

ciWiringSuggestion: python3 tests/Packaging.Domain/test_release_results.py -v before the native-build command in the already-authorized Task-07 helper. This is the focused regression for this concrete defect, not another product matrix.
limits: This source GO does not pass B24, the pristine consumer, runtime transfer, compatibility, package publication/rollback or actual CI. Those existing checks must run on final candidate C.

The two result files are individually atomically replaced, not a cross-file transaction. Their ordering and the final top-level commit marker make interrupted states nonterminal; no durability beyond the existing atomic writer is asserted.
No historical B22/B23 replay or new acceptance gate is requested.
